Scope: phase 1 of the logistics area. Wet networks (sewerage, storm, potable water, fire fighting and TSE, including the force main), dry networks (medium voltage, low voltage, street lighting and telecom), the potable water pump station, the sewage lift station, guard rooms, all road layers up to the asphalt wearing course, and landscape.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At the 03-Nov-2026 data date the project is 62.1% complete against 80.1% planned, 18.0% behind the plan (SPI 0.78). It gained 1.4% this week against 4.1% planned, so the gap widened from 15.3% to 18.0%.

With 84.1% of the contract time gone, 37.9% of the work remains. Finishing by the contract completion date of 29-Jan-2027 needs about 3.2% a week over the 12 whole weeks left, against 1.4% achieved this week. The weekly report's milestone sheet and the P6 update now forecast project handover on 15-Mar-2027, 45 days late, a week later again than last week's forecast. Construction is the weak phase: 52.5% done against 84.3% planned.

Wet networks and street lighting moved mostPotable water pipes rose by 480 LM to 88.6%, storm pipes by 309 LM to 97.3% and fire-fighting pipes by 197 LM to 99.6%. Street-light cable rose by 1,156 LM to 28.6% and MV cable by 399 LM to 47.1%.

The P6 update finishes the project on 15-Mar-2027, 45 days after the contract completion date. Most P6 milestones moved another 7 days later with the data date; storm water now finishes earlier (28-Nov-2026, previously 06-Dec-2026) and potable water stays at 05-Dec-2026. The schedule has no finish constraint at the contract date, so its float is measured against its own late finish. The asphalt wearing course has 5 days of float and construction finish 10 days. Other forecasts in this week's files: 28-Feb-2027 (General Information sheet), 20-Dec-2026 (recovery schedule in the progress presentation) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet).

Data notes

  • Report week: the weekly report states "Current Contract Weeks: 66 of 78" (Milestones sheet). The report serial number (WPR048) and the consultant's inspection number (48) are not the week number.
  • This-week values compare this report with the 27-Oct-2026 report (previous week folder).
  • Four different completion forecasts: 28-Feb-2027 (General Information sheet, −30 days), 15-Mar-2027 (Milestones sheet and P6 update, −45 days), 20-Dec-2026 (recovery schedule in the progress presentation) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet and the presentation's "target" date).
  • The P6 update has no finish constraint, so no activity shows negative float although it finishes after the contract date. 319 in-progress activities have finish dates before the data date.
  • Monthly actuals in the Physical-Chart Data sheet change every week: last week they were lowered, this week raised above their earlier values (May 29.6%, July 40.8%, September 50.3%).
  • Quantities and man-hours disagree: Major Quantities adds 175 LM of LV cable this week, but the LV network earned no man-hours.
  • The November head count is not entered in the Manpower sheet (0). For October, the front page shows 360 planned and 483 actual labour; the Manpower sheet shows 78 and 537.
  • Mobilisation: the weekly report gives 30-Aug-2025 as actual, the P6 milestone "Mobilization - Finish" gives 25-Nov-2025.
  • The "Complete earthworks" forecast of 08-Sep-2026 has passed but is still marked as a forecast, with earthworks at 96.2%. The "all materials delivered" forecast of 07-Nov-2026 conflicts with 46 of 160 materials not yet on site.
  • Procurement: the civil and roads material count rose from 77 to 82 without explanation. The workbook's procurement log is still unusable and its front-page total still repeats the mechanical row. The procurement presentation lists 5 RMUs against 3 elsewhere, 377 street-light poles delivered against 380 on the lighting slide, and 13 fire hydrants against 12; the substations' date of 30-Oct-2026 has passed without change.
  • NCRs: the front page shows 4 issued and 3 closed; the Quality-Stat sheet shows 51 issued and 51 closed.
  • Sewer pipes are 89.9% finished in Major Quantities, 110.7% in the Conclusion sheet (6,804 of 6,146 LM) and 100% in the presentation (6,257 of 6,257 LM). Fire-fighting pipes are 100.9% in the Conclusion sheet.
  • Cumulative toolbox-talk attendance fell from 9,091 to 4,091 between the two reports.
  • Contract value is 198,906,162.61 on the front page and 198,906,162.312 "incl. VAT" in the Conclusion sheet. The invoice log has stray values (21,100,000, 20,900,000, 200,000) and EAC shows #REF!.
  • Key submittal dates are in Feb–Mar 2024, before the contract award of 30-Jun-2025. The look-ahead sheet contains P6 data from the Hail Industrial City Phase II project, and the risk register uses project ID DAM2-01-029 and names the 3rd and 6th Industrial Cities.
  • The workbook's issue 1 text still quotes 304 workers and 184 items of equipment; the presentation gives 537 workers and 306 items of equipment.
  • The workbook's front page and the presentation also report cost-based progress; this report uses physical progress only.
